## Claims
- [source-backed] arXiv:0809.2981v2 formally states: for \(v=v_{r,s,t,n}\) with \(\mathfrak S_v=s_{i^j}\), \(a=\min(n-r-i,r-j)\), \(b=\min(i,j)\), \(J_v\) is generated as an ideal of \(H^\star(G/P_J,\mathbb Z)\cong\Lambda/I_{r,n-r}\) by either \(\{s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq((i+a)^b,i^{j-b})\}\) or \(\{s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq(i^j,b^a)\}\). [source-2, lines 1382-1402]
- [source-backed] The same source gives a general graded-module proposition over a commutative ring \(R\), then specializes to symmetric functions with \(\mathbb Z\)-coefficients and \(M=J_{v_{r,s,t,n}}\). [source-2, lines 1522-1540]
- [source-backed] The supplied arXiv excerpts do not state an equality identifying \(J_v\) as an exact integral \(\mathbb Z\)-span of a specified Schur family. The earlier definition instead says \(J_v:=\Bbbk\)-span of \(\{\sigma_u:u\ge v\}\), without specifying \(\Bbbk\) in that excerpt. [source-2, lines 328-337]
- [source-backed] Provider metadata identifies the later paper as Avery St. Dizier and Alexander Yong, “Presenting the cohomology of a Schubert variety: Proof of the minimality conjecture,” DOI \(10.1112/jlms.12832\); its abstract says it proves the minimality conjecture using the Hopf-algebra structure of symmetric functions. [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832]
- [source-backed] The retrieved later DOI and arXiv:2209.02011v2 records supply abstract-level material only; neither contains exact theorem text giving an integral Schur-span description of \(J_v\), nor precise coefficient hypotheses. [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832] [arxiv:2209.02011v2]
- [unsupported] No conclusion about the later paper’s exact theorem statement, its coefficient ring, or an integral Schur-span presentation follows from the retrieved abstracts.

## Strategy
Separate the original formal arXiv theorem—which explicitly uses \(\mathbb Z\)—from the requested stronger integral Schur-span equality. Treat the later-paper records as metadata/abstract leads only.

## Gaps
The later paper’s full text and theorem locators were not retrieved. The bounded record set therefore cannot establish or refute whether its full text contains the requested statement.

## Next
Retrieve a theorem-level excerpt from DOI \(10.1112/jlms.12832\) or arXiv:2209.02011v2 before making any claim about its integral hypotheses or exact \(J_v\) Schur-span formulation.
